newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: ASEAN hopes to work out Cambodia ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN hopes to work out Cambodia ceasefire.

text.p: The Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) will try to work out a ceasefire in Cambodia during talks with Cambodian leaders, Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Friday.

ASEAN has set up a mission composed of the foreign ministers of the Philippines, Thailand and Indonesia to meet Cambodian head of state King Norodom Sihanouk and the country's two rival prime ministers to resolve the Cambodian crisis. "To try to get some arrangement or formula to improve the situation so that you have peace, ceasefire -- real ceasefire," Siazon told reporters when asked what the objective of the mission was.

ASEAN has decided to postpone Cambodia's membership in the association but said it will go ahead and accept Laos and Burma as new members during a meeting of its foreign minister in Kuala Lumpur later this month. Siazon said he could not say if ASEAN would still accept Cambodia despite the internal disorder in that country. "Anything is possible," he said when asked whether a change in the ASEAN position on Cambodia's membership was possible before the Kuala Lumpur meeting.

At least 58 people were killed and up to 200 wounded when Second Prime Minister Hun Sen's troops took control of Phnom Penh in fighting with forces of First Prime Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh last weekend.
